{
  "screen_decision": "exclude",
  "screen_rationale": "The study proposes guidelines for reporting animal research (ARRIVE) and discusses the importance of good reporting for the scientific process. It does not report any quantitative measure of agreement between animal model results and human clinical outcomes, nor does it analyze any specific animal model's concordance with human data. The text focuses on methodology and reporting standards, not on evaluating the predictive value of animal models.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "The text discusses the relevance of animal models to human biology and the limitations of animal models used in studies.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The ARRIVE guidelines are presented as applicable to 'any area of bioscience research using laboratory animals', indicating a broad, cross-cutting application.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The text discusses the application of the ARRIVE guidelines to 'any area of bioscience research using laboratory animals' and refers to 'published animal research' and 'research using animals' generally, implying a broad scope across various model types.",
  "species": [
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The text refers to 'laboratory animals' and 'any species of animal undergoing an experimental procedure' without specifying or analyzing any particular species.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The text mentions reporting of 'experimental outcomes' and 'molecular markers' as part of the ARRIVE guidelines, which are typically considered secondary biomarkers."
}
